ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit is a 5 V voltage source, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. On the top there is a 1Ω resistor connecting the upper-left node and the upper-right node; on the bottom there is a 1Ω resistor connecting the lower-left node and the lower-right node. In the figure there are also two crossing diagonal branches, each diagonal branch is labeled with a 1Ω resistor. The vertical branch on the right side has a 2Ω resistor connected between the upper-right node and the lower-right node, with the current i marked downward beside it. Reasoning: Take the upper-right node and the lower-right node in the figure as the bridge nodes connected by the 2Ω resistor. Viewed from the two ends of the 5 V source, one path is composed of two 1Ω resistors in series, and the other crossing path is also composed of two 1Ω resistors in series; the resistance ratios on the two sides are the same, and the bridge network is balanced. Therefore the potentials of the upper-right and lower-right bridge nodes are equal, and the voltage across the 2Ω resistor is 0. By Ohm's law i = 0/2Ω = 0 A.

method.method_draft: First read the image topology, then assign node voltages: let the source upper-left node be 5 V and lower-left node be 0 V. Let V_B and V_C be the top and bottom terminals of the 2Ω resistor. Write KCL at B and C; because each node has one 1Ω connection to 5 V, one 1Ω connection to 0 V, and the same 2Ω connection between them, subtracting the two KCL equations gives V_B = V_C. Hence the voltage across the 2Ω resistor is zero, so i = (V_B - V_C)/2Ω = 0 A.
